title: Hosted API - Embeddings + Rerank Demo
next_steps: Share security whitepaper and SOC2 report
Schedule a follow-up POC scoping call week of 6/29
action_items: Avery Li: Share hosted pricing and dedicated vs hosted TCO spreadsheet (due: 2026-06-20)
Diego Morales: Run a 10k query benchmark on ShopZen sample dataset and share results (due: 2026-06-24)
Tom Alvarez: Provide sample dataset and top-k labels for relevance scoring (due: 2026-06-21)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked the ShopZen search team through Hosted API embeddings and rerank endpoints. Demo covered embedding pipeline, ANN vs brute-force rerank, HTTP/SDK examples, Console walkthrough for routing and Optimize suggestions. Customer constraints: sub-150ms p99 for search, cost sensitivity at scale, SOC2 requirement and SSO/SAML. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, sample benchmark and POC scoping.
transcript:
00:00 Avery Li: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Avery from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Diego (SE) and Janelle from CS. how's everybody doing?
00:07 Rachel Kim: Good, thanks. Excited to see embeddings + rerank, we've been evaluating a few options.
00:12 Diego Morales: cool, we'll keep it practical — show the hosted API path for embeddings, discuss the two-stage rerank flow, and run through the console and Optimize suggestions. if something comes up interrupt.
00:20 Tom Alvarez: quick note, our current stack is elasticsearch backed by a custom ANN, we have per-query latency SLO of 150ms p99 and about 1.2M queries per day peak, just so you know.
00:33 Avery Li: perfect, that's helpful. Rachel, are you owning the relevance metric? what are you optimizing for — ctr, session conversion?
00:39 Rachel Kim: mainly conversion and time-to-purchase, we use nDCG-ish metrics internally, plus some manual labeling for top results. we also have a lot of tail queries with product aliases.
00:47 Diego Morales: ok, great. so we'll demo a typical flow: index -> embeddings -> ANN search -> reranker call to Redwood Hosted Rerank endpoint which scores the top-k results and returns re-ranked list. we'll point out latency windows and cost implications.
01:02 Priya Singh: quick question on data residency and retention — we need logs and audit trails stored for 1 year, and SSO via SAML.
01:10 Avery Li: yes, we support SAML SSO for the console, and audit logs with retention options; I'll share the security whitepaper and our SOC 2 report after.
01:18 Rachel Kim: perfect. ok show us the API.
01:22 Diego Morales: switching to the demo. (screen share) here's the hosted embeddings endpoint call: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, we show the JSON payload. for ecomm we often recommend 1024-dim models or 768 depending on downstream cost.
01:38 Tom Alvarez: do you have recommendations on dimension vs latency? we can't blow up token cost.
01:43 Diego Morales: yes — higher dims give more nuance but increase storage and ANN index size; tradeoff is retrieval quality vs storage/ANN ops. Optimize can analyze your workload and suggest a quantized profile, e.g., 384–512 dims is often sweet for product catalogs.
01:58 Rachel Kim: how about realtime indexing? we have merchants adding products constantly.
02:03 Diego Morales: we support async batch and near-realtime incremental indexing; embedding generation can be run at ingestion and cached. Redwood's prefix/KV caching helps if you re-query similar content.
02:14 Avery Li: also note hosted API has auto-scaling; if you want guaranteed throughput we'd talk about Dedicated.
02:20 Priya Singh: dedicated would be interesting if it reduces cost at steady load.
02:24 Diego Morales: cool. now the rerank flow: after ANN we call POST /v1/rerank with candidate set, we pass query embedding plus candidates (text + metadata) and the model outputs relevance scores which we use to reorder.
02:40 Tom Alvarez: is rerank model hosted or does it call your inference runtime? what's the underlying model?
02:44 Diego Morales: it's hosted on Redwood's runtime, typically a lightweight instruction-tuned encoder-decoder or cross-encoder variant we've benchmarked for rerank. you can choose tradeoffs — a smaller cross-encoder for low latency or larger for accuracy; we provide performance profiles.
02:58 Rachel Kim: what's typical p50/p99 for rerank on hosted?
03:01 Diego Morales: for small candidate sets (top 10–50), we've seen p50 ~20–40ms and p99 ~90–150ms depending on model size and sequence length; you can push lower with batching or a smaller model.
03:17 Priya Singh: we're aiming for end-to-end p99 <150ms; that includes ANN time + rerank.
03:23 Diego Morales: it's achievable with a tuned ANN + a compact reranker. Optimize can recommend batching windows, caching TTLs, and quantization. we'll show the console.
03:33 (screen flicker)
03:36 Diego Morales: here is the Redwood Console — routes page. you can define a route for search queries that points to a chain: embedding -> ANN -> rerank. route-level metrics show per-token cost, latency breakdown, and token counts.
03:51 Rachel Kim: nice, can we see historical deltas after a model change?
03:55 Diego Morales: yes, the console shows pre/post rollout metrics and A/B results if you do a canary. we also hook to your evals so you can run prompt sets to measure regressions.
04:05 Tom Alvarez: do you provide tools to compute recall/precision over a labeled set?
04:09 Diego Morales: we do — evals integration and automated regression alerts tied to prompt sets or labeled test sets.
04:13 Rachel Kim: earlier you mentioned caching — will caching bias results for personalization?
04:17 Diego Morales: caching is prefix/KV based — safe defaults are per-session or per-query canonicalize; personalization uses user-specific signals in reranker features rather than naive cache. you configure it per route.
04:29 Avery Li: quick aside, any competitors you saw in your eval?
04:31 Tom Alvarez: we've been testing Pinecone and Elastic + custom rerank. Pinecone is fast but we found rerank quality varied.
04:39 Diego Morales: understoood. we often recommend hybrid approach: ANN for recall then rerank for precise ordering.
04:44 Rachel Kim: can you show a code example for embedding + ANN + rerank?
04:48 Diego Morales: sure. (switch to code) Step 1: call embeddings endpoint, store vectors in your ANN. Step 2: query ANN for top-k. Step 3: call /v1/rerank with the candidate list and query text. we'll show a sample Node/python snippet.
05:08 (diego scrolls)
05:12 Diego Morales: note the rerank payload includes metadata so your model can use filters like category, price bands. here's an example of passing product attributes.
05:25 Priya Singh: that helps. does hosted API support encrypted-at-rest keys that we control?
05:29 Avery Li: yes, customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM is supported on Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have managed keys but we can discuss HSM integrations under enterprise terms.
05:42 Tom Alvarez: we have compliance constraints; any issues with sending product titles or user signals to the hosted API?
05:47 Avery Li: by default hosted keeps data for 30 days for telemetry; enterprise customers can opt for zero-retention modes or Dedicated/Private for no-telemetry; I'll add the exact retention policy in the security doc I share.
05:59 Rachel Kim: are there rate limits? burst handling?
06:02 Diego Morales: hosted has per-account rate limits, bursts are smoothed by autoscaler; for spikes we recommend burst capacity or Dedicated. we'll include quotas in the pricing sheet.
06:11 Rachel Kim: let's look at a live rerank example.
06:14 Diego Morales: sending a sample query. (types) here the ANN returned 50 candidates, rerank call scores and reorders — see the score deltas, previous top item gets pushed to 3. you can log the features to debug.
06:28 Tom Alvarez: I notice some transcription artifacts in your example — sorry I mean some mismatches, are tokenization differences important?
06:34 Diego Morales: tokenization can affect embeddings slightly, but models normalize common tokens; we provide consistent tokenizer libs to reduce differences.
06:41 Rachel Kim: curious about cost — what's unit economics for our scale? 1.2M q/day with average 12 tokens per query and 20 tokens in rerank etc.
06:49 Avery Li: I'll run numbers and send TCO. hosted pricing is per-embedding call + per-rerank call. Optimize can show where batching and caching could save up to 30–60% on token costs for repeated queries. Also quantized models reduce compute cost.
07:08 Priya Singh: Realistically, if we wanted a POC, what would it look like?
07:12 Avery Li: typical POC: 2–4 week pilot using hosted API, we run a benchmark with your sample dataset, evaluate metrics (nDCG, p99 latency), and then propose Dedicated sizing if steady-state benefits warrant it.
07:22 Tom Alvarez: we might prefer starting hosted to iterate fast.
07:25 Rachel Kim: agreed. can you show Optimize recommendations?
07:28 Diego Morales: switching to Optimize tab — it analyzes request traces and suggests batching windows, cache TTLs, and model quantization levels per route. here it suggests for search: 50ms batching window, 384-dim quantized profile for embeddings, and a smaller cross-encoder for reranker during peak.
07:46 Rachel Kim: 50ms batching — won't that add latency?
07:48 Diego Morales: batching trades immediate p50 for lower p99 and cost efficiency; Optimize suggests a sweet spot depending on traffic shape. you can have mixed strategies: latency-sensitive routes without batching, cost-sensitive routes with batching.
07:59 Priya Singh: what about on-prem? some of our enterprise buyers will ask.
08:02 Avery Li: Private (VPC/on-prem) is available — same API/console but deployed in your network; audit logs and KMS integrate. that's typically later stage.
08:12 Tom Alvarez: any limits on candidate set size for reranker?
08:15 Diego Morales: we recommend top-k 50–200 — larger candidate sets increase rerank compute; sometimes we use a filter-first step to reduce candidates.
08:25 Rachel Kim: ok, love the console metrics. last thing: will we be able to compare different rerank models easily?
08:30 Diego Morales: yes, model rollouts and A/B testing are built in; you can compare metrics and have automatic rollback if quality drops.
08:38 Avery Li: quick recap: we'll send pricing/TCO and security docs, Diego will run benchmark on sample data once Tom shares it, and we'll set up a POC scoping call — any additions?
08:53 Rachel Kim: please include an example notebook and the step-by-step indexer.
08:57 Janelle Park: noted, will include onboarding checklist and a sample benchmark notebook.
09:02 Tom Alvarez: timeline — can you schedule the scoping call in the week of 6/29?
09:06 Avery Li: yes we'll propose times. thanks everyone.
09:10 Rachel Kim: thanks, that was helpful.
09:12 (call ends)
